text: For an excessively salty dish or soup, if a dish is too salty, add unsalted ingredients or liquid, then taste again. Acid or fat can balance perception but does not remove salt. Do not rely on adding sugar alone.

For an overly spicy curry or too-hot dish, to tame chili heat, add more unsalted base, yogurt or dairy if compatible, coconut milk, or a little sweetness. Check the recipe and dietary requirements first.
For an overly watery sauce, to fix watery sauce, simmer uncovered to reduce it. A starch slurry, roux, pureed vegetables, or tomato paste may help depending on the dish.
For a separated sauce, reduce heat; whisk the broken sauce slowly into a small amount of a fresh compatible emulsion base, such as water or mustard.
Baking relies on ingredient roles such as structure, moisture, leavening, fat, and sweetness. Ingredient substitutions can change texture, so use tested replacements.
Vegan swaps may include unsweetened plant milk for milk, coconut or cashew cream for cream, and plant butter for butter. Check allergens carefully.
Keep perishable foods refrigerated promptly; verify safe cooking and storage temperatures against authoritative food-safety guidance, not just recipe instructions.
